reports.report: The problem is equivalent to finding the maximum number of colors in an $n \times n$ grid such that no $2 \times 2$ block contains 4 distinct colors. This is achieved by minimizing the number of pairs of squares of the same color needed to cover all $(n-1)^2$ possible $2 \times 2$ blocks. Since each pair of adjacent squares can cover at most 2 blocks, the minimum number of pairs required is $\lceil (n-1)^2 / 2 \rceil$. For $n=100$, there are $99^2 = 9801$ blocks, requiring $\lceil 9801 / 2 \rceil = 4901$ pairs. The maximum number of colors is $100^2 - 4901 = 5099$.
